reason: Conversation 2 asks about the code and make, identifies the new drawer as the key clue, and when the customer refuses to look, gives a clear verdict (probably the gap, not the fan) and says who to call (an engineer or the kitchen fitter to check clearance). Conversation 1 keeps asking a customer who has refused to inspect anything to hunt for vents and pull the drawer out, and its formatting is garbled. It also leans toward 'fan motor failing, needs replacement part' without justification and never names who to call, though it does usefully advise switching off and letting the hob cool.
